newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Key Indonesia NGO attacks minister's threat.
newsitem.headline: Key Indonesia NGO attacks minister's threat.

text.p: A key private Indonesian organisation on Saturday attacked a minister's statement threatening to take action against "problem" NGOs as an act of scaremongering designed to undermine activists groups.

The Indonesian Legal Aid Foundation (LBH) attacked a statement made on Friday by Coordinating Minister for Politics Susilo Sudarman that Indonesia planned take action against 32 non-government organisation (NGOs) regarded as posing problems.
"The criteria for those posing a problem are those that do not use the state ideology Pancasila as the basis for their organisation and conduct illegal activities," Sudarman said.
The five principles of Pancasila include belief in one God, humanitarianism, national unity, democracy through consensus, and social justice.

Bambang Widjojanto, head of the LBH, said: "We are seeing a pattern of accusations which have the intention of recycling fear in the community and have the consequence of harming the credibility of all NGOs."

"As a consequence (of the statement), the community will be even more scared to put forward its social, political and cultural aspirations. This is a backward step for the development of a national life which is humanitarian and civilised," he said.

Widjojanto said Sudarman's statement, which did not name the 32 organisations, was "provocative" and called on the minister to give a concrete example of what he meant by "problem NGOs" and to explain the basis for such accusations.

Following the crackdown on NGOs after the July riots in Jakarta, the LBH, which is helping defend all those arrested by authorities, is one of the few activist groups which continues to speak out publicly.

NGOs have complained to the official National Human Rights Commission that they have been harassed and intimidated by security agencies. Fearing official reprisals, many outspoken groups have curtailed their activities or gone underground since the crackdown.
After the riots, regarded as the worst in more than 20 years, the government said it would re-register all NGOs.
